situation:
You are the operations manager for MORNING LINE COFFEE CO-OPERATIVE, a breakfast-and-coffee drive-thru company with six stores. The co-operative is owned by the sixty people who work in it, and the member-owners each take a share of the profit each quarter. The general manager (judge) has asked you for a recommendation on a problem the members raised at their last meeting.

Nearly all of the co-operative's sales go out through the drive-thru window in a ninety-minute morning wave. Orders from customers with allergies, asking for food prepared away from wheat, dairy, peanuts or sesame, have tripled in two years. The kitchen is small, its boards are shared, and the same tongs move between the biscuit line and the egg line.

Last month a crew member handed a customer with a sesame allergy a sandwich built on a board that had just held seed bread. Nobody was hurt, and the customer wrote to the members anyway. Cross-contact is now a risk the co-operative carries at every store, and a crew working that fast is not a crew working safely.

One path moves allergen orders off the window onto the mobile app with a lead time. That protects the kitchen, but gives up the customers who order at the drive-thru without planning ahead, leaving them the packaged snacks beside the coffee. The other path is to staff a sealed allergen prep station, which takes a member off the line at the rush, pushes window times up, and throws out short-dated sealed ingredients.

The general manager (judge) wants a recommendation on how the co-operative should handle allergen orders, and the members must vote on any change that adds a position to a shift. You will present in the back office. The general manager (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the general manager's questions, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager (judge) of MORNING LINE COFFEE CO-OPERATIVE. Business background is the same as the situation above. You want the operations manager to recommend how the co-operative should handle allergen orders at its six drive-thru stores, and to be plain about what that recommendation costs the members, the crew and the customers who order with allergies.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what will this have done to our window times?
If allergen orders keep growing the way they have, does your recommendation still hold?
